blocks.content: Every Judge of a High Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State, and, in the case of appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the High Court.

items: High Court judges are appointed by the President, not the Governor, although the Governor of the state is consulted.
Unlike Supreme Court judges, a 'distinguished jurist' category is NOT a valid qualification for appointment as a High Court judge under Article 217.
The retirement age of High Court judges was raised from 60 to 62 years by the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1963.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Every High Court Judge is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
The President must consult the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the state concerned before making an appointment.
In the appointment of a judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the respective High Court is also consulted.
Qualifications require Indian citizenship and 10 years of holding judicial office or 10 years as an advocate in a High Court.
A High Court Judge holds office until reaching the age of 62 years.
